value.body:
Editing a merged pull request can update its record on the author's PDS while leaving the appview unchanged.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Create and merge a pull request.
2. As the pull request author, use the pencil button to edit its title or body.
3. Save the edit.
4. Reload the pull request page and inspect the pull record on the author's PDS.

The web page continues to show the old title and body, even when the PDS record was updated successfully.

The edit handler writes the updated record to the PDS and then calls `db.PutPull`. However, `db.PutPull` returns without updating the appview database when the existing pull state is `PullMerged`:

```go
if existingPull.State == models.PullMerged {
    return nil
}
```

This leaves the PDS and appview with different pull request contents. It also makes reference changes derived from the edited body invisible in the web UI.

Expected behavior:

- either merged pull requests remain editable and the appview reflects those metadata changes; or
- editing is consistently disabled before any PDS write is attempted.

Relevant paths:

- `appview/pulls/edit.go`
- `appview/db/pulls.go`
- `appview/pages/templates/repo/pulls/fragments/pullHeader.html`

Related:

- [#405: proposal: move db logic to ingester](https://tangled.org/tangled.org/core/issues/405), which discusses eliminating handler-side PDS/appview double writes.
- `proposal: appview atproto reconciler` (`at://did:plc:xasnlahkri4ewmbuzly2rlc5/sh.tangled.repo.issue/3mjdmzxgeup22`), which proposes detecting and repairing PDS/appview divergence.
value.title: Editing a merged pull updates the PDS but not the appview

value.body: [This page](https://tangled.org/mrichardson.tngl.sh/home.6t.lt/tree/main/jq-html-home/data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,) on the main tangled website currently contains a broken link which leads to a 503 response. The page links to a directory within my git repository, and that directory contains "?" (U+003F) in the name. The link is fixed by encoding the question mark as "%3F". I had the same issue with an unencoded "#" (U+0023) as well. I don't know what code is responsible for encoding the URLs, so I'm not sure if other characters would cause similar issues.
value.title: Characters left unencoded in URLs
